title: Roofing Realty Inspection Report
template_description: Professional roofing inspection using a streamlined 4-step narrated video workflow: Overview (general roof qualities + many wide shots), Components (penetrations & mounted equipment), Substrates (roof materials, construction & field damage), and Misc (supplemental data for future use). Zero computer vision — powered by precise STT timestamps + agentic LLM reasoning over your spoken observations. Produces clean, client-ready PDFs with extracted still frames, severity badges, and professional recommendations.
domain_expert_standards: NRCA roofing practices, ASTM roof condition assessment, IBC/IRC roofing provisions, and manufacturer installation standards for shingle, TPO, EPDM, metal, and modified-bitumen systems. Conclusions are drawn only from narrated observations.

pdf_styling.page_footer: Confidential · Structured Roofing Systems · Page {page} of {total_pages}
pdf_styling.cover_subtitle: Professional roof inspection — Overview • Components • Substrates
pdf_styling.disclaimer_text: This inspection report reflects visible and readily accessible roof conditions at the time of the guided field video inspection. It is a professional opinion only and is not a warranty, guarantee, structural engineering certification, or prediction of future performance. Latent or concealed defects may exist. All repair recommendations should be verified and performed by a licensed roofing contractor. Remaining life estimates are approximate and assume normal weather and maintenance.

guidance.intro_script: Welcome to the Roofing Realty Inspection with Structured Roofing Systems. We will document the roof using a clear 4-step workflow. First: Overview — capture the general qualities of the entire roof with many wide shots from all angles and slopes. Second: Components — document anything that penetrates or is mounted on the roof. Third: Substrates — show the actual roof materials, how the roof is built, and any damage to the construction. Fourth: Miscellaneous — capture anything else useful for future reports or deeper analysis (this section is stored separately and will not appear in the main body of this report). At every stop, hold steady, say “Mark this.” clearly, then describe exactly what you are showing. Speak in complete sentences. Safety first at all times.
guidance.outro_script: Inspection complete. Thank you for the detailed narration across Overview, Components, Substrates, and Misc. Upload this video to generate your professional PDF report. The Misc section has been captured for future use.

sections.title: Overview
sections.voice_prompt: This is the Overview step. Film wide establishing shots of the entire roof from as many safe angles and vantage points as possible — front, rear, both sides, ridge views, eave views, and any different slopes or roof sections. You can easily take 10 to 15 photos here. Say “Mark this.” after each significant wide shot or change in angle. Narrate the general qualities of the roof: overall profile and shape, number of slopes or planes, general condition impression from a distance, any obvious major features or issues visible from the ground, and how the roof sits on the building. This section is only about the big picture and general qualities — do not zoom in on specific components or materials yet.
sections.on_screen_text:
OVERVIEW
Wide shots from all angles & slopes • General roof profile & qualities
(10–15 photos encouraged)
sections.worker_instructions: Walk the full perimeter of the building (or all safe vantage points) and capture the WHOLE roof, not close-ups. For each new angle or slope, hold the camera steady for 2–3 seconds, say “Mark this.”, then describe what you see in a full sentence (e.g. “This is the front slope, a moderately pitched gable in fair overall condition”). You are done when every visible roof plane has at least one wide shot and you have described the overall profile, the number of slopes, and your general condition impression. Do NOT zoom into vents, seams, or damage yet — that comes later.
success_criteria: At least 8 wide establishing shots covering every visible roof plane/slope.
Spoken description of overall roof profile, shape, and number of slopes.
A stated general condition impression from a distance (e.g. good/fair/poor).
No close-up component or material shots in this step.

sections.title: Components
sections.voice_prompt: This is the Components step. Document every structure or item that penetrates the roof surface or is mounted on top of the roof. This includes HVAC units and curbs, skylights, chimneys, flues, satellite dishes, antennas, solar panels, vents, pipes, roof jacks, and any other mounted or penetrating equipment. For each significant item, get a clear shot and say “Mark this.” then describe: what the item is, its location on the roof, its condition, how it is flashed or sealed to the roof, and any visible issues (leaks, rust, poor flashing, damage, etc.). Mark each important component separately.
sections.on_screen_text:
COMPONENTS
Penetrations & mounted equipment
HVAC • Skylights • Chimneys • Antennas • Vents • Solar • etc.
sections.worker_instructions: Move across the roof and stop at EVERY penetration or mounted item. Mark each one separately — do not lump two vents into one mark. For each, say “Mark this.” then state four things: (1) what it is, (2) where it is on the roof, (3) its condition, and (4) how it is flashed/sealed and whether that flashing looks sound. Call out leaks, rust, cracked boots, or lifted flashing explicitly. You are done when there are no un-documented penetrations or mounted items left on the roof.
success_criteria: One separate mark per significant penetration or mounted item.
Each item's type, location, and condition stated aloud.
Flashing/sealing condition described for each item.
Any leak, rust, or flashing failure explicitly called out.

sections.title: Substrates
sections.voice_prompt: This is the Substrates step. Show the actual materials the roof is made of and how it is constructed. Some roofs have multiple materials — document each type. Film close-ups and representative areas of shingles, TPO, EPDM, metal panels (R-panel, standing seam, etc.), modified bitumen, built-up, or any other substrate. Also capture construction details: seams, laps, fasteners, insulation if visible, slope transitions, and especially any damage to the roof material itself (splits, tears, punctures, granule loss in context of the material, blistering, seam failure, etc.). Say “Mark this.” for each important material area or damage example and describe what the roof is made of, how it was built, and the current condition of the materials and construction.
sections.on_screen_text:
SUBSTRATES
Roof materials • Construction details • Seams • Field damage & condition
(Shingles • Metal • TPO • Rubber • etc.)
sections.worker_instructions: Get in close on the roof field itself. Capture a representative close-up of EACH material type present (if the roof mixes materials, document each one). For every material area or damage example, say “Mark this.” then describe: what the material is, how it is put together (seams, laps, fasteners, transitions), and its current condition. Deliberately hunt for and mark field damage — splits, tears, punctures, blistering, seam failure, granule loss — and describe its location and extent. You are done when every material type is documented and any visible field damage has its own marked close-up.
success_criteria: A representative close-up of every roof material type present.
Construction details (seams, laps, fasteners, transitions) described.
Each area of field damage marked and described with location/extent.
At least 4 substrate marks for a typical roof.

sections.title: Miscellaneous / Supplemental
sections.voice_prompt: This is the Miscellaneous step. Use it to capture any additional items, context, notes, or observations that may be useful for generating future reports or for deeper analysis later. This can include site conditions, drainage away from the building, nearby trees, access limitations, client comments, or anything else not covered in Overview, Components, or Substrates. Say “Mark this.” and describe what you are capturing and why it might be useful later. Note: This section is stored for future use and will NOT be used to generate the main sections of this specific report.
sections.on_screen_text:
MISC / SUPPLEMENTAL
Anything else useful for future reports or analysis
(Not included in this report's main body)
sections.worker_instructions: Optional catch-all. If there is anything worth recording that did not fit Overview, Components, or Substrates — drainage, grading, overhanging trees, access limitations, or a client comment — say “Mark this.” and explain what it is and why it may matter later. If nothing applies, you can skip this step; it is not required. Nothing captured here appears in the main body of the report.
success_criteria: Any relevant supplemental item is marked with a spoken explanation of why it matters.
It is acceptable to record zero marks here (the step is optional).

sections.title: Overview
sections.default_text: General roof profile, slopes, and overall qualities were documented through multiple wide establishing shots. No spoken findings were recorded beyond the visual walkthrough for this area.

field_specs.label: Key general observations from wide views

sections.writer_instructions: Write a professional big-picture summary of the roof based only on the wide overview narration and photos. Describe the overall profile, number and orientation of slopes/planes, general shape on the building, and the overall visual condition and maintenance impression from a distance. Note any obvious major features visible from the ground. Keep this high-level — do not drill into specific components or material details (those come in later sections). Use neutral professional language suitable for a real estate or maintenance report. Do not invent details not present in the narration.

sections.title: Components
sections.default_text: Roof penetrations and mounted equipment were documented per technician narration. Where narration was limited, the still frames should be reviewed directly.
sections.writer_instructions: Create a clear, organized summary of all roof penetrations and mounted equipment documented. List each significant component (HVAC, skylights, chimneys, antennas, vents, solar, etc.) with its location and observed condition. Note flashing/sealing quality and any issues (leaks, rust, poor installation, damage). Group similar items if many. Elevate severity for items creating active or high-risk water intrusion. Recommendations should be specific and practical. Professional neutral tone for realty or repair planning use. When several items are marked, address each in photo order rather than lumping them together.

sections.title: Substrates
sections.default_text: Roof materials, construction details, and condition of the roof field were documented per technician narration. Where narration was limited, the still frames should be reviewed directly.

field_specs.label: Recommended actions for roof materials & construction

sections.writer_instructions: Provide a factual, detailed summary of the roof substrates and construction. Clearly identify all material types present (shingles, TPO, metal panels, EPDM, modified bitumen, etc.) and note if the roof uses multiple substrates. Describe visible construction details (seams, laps, fastening, transitions). Document any damage to the roof materials or construction itself (splits, tears, punctures, seam failure, blistering, granule loss patterns, etc.) with locations and extent. Tie severity to impact on watertightness and remaining service life. Recommendations should address root causes (e.g. seam repair method, material-specific fixes). Professional neutral to advisory tone.

sections.title: Miscellaneous / Supplemental Data
sections.default_text: No supplemental observations were captured for future use during this inspection.
sections.writer_instructions: This section contains supplemental data captured for future report generation or deeper analysis and is not part of the main report body for this inspection. Provide a brief, neutral summary of what was documented in the Misc section. List key items or observations without forcing them into the main narrative. If nothing significant was captured, state that clearly using the default_text. Use 'informational' severity unless the content clearly warrants higher. Keep this section light and factual.
